newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goldfields lowers year profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goldfields lowers year profit forecast.

text.p: Goldfields Ltd said on Wednesday it had lowered its forecast for net profit before abnormals for the year to June 30 to between A$10 million to A$15 million.
The downgrade follows an earlier revised forecast of net profit after abnormals for the year within the range of A$20 million to A$25 million in late August last year.

Goldfields said the principal reason for the lastest downgrade was lower production from its 25 percent owned Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea due to difficult mining conditions, lower than anticipated equipment availability and reduced plant recoveries. The company also said output from its Henty gold mine in Tasmania was lower than expected because of delays in accessing the mine's high grade ore body.

Goldfields said other negative factors were the lower price of gold and higher interest costs because of lower operational cash flow. "However since the earlier forecast Goldfields has negotiated the sale of its tenements at Wau in Papua New Guinea, which is expected to generate an abnormal profit in the order of A$8 million in the second half of the year," the company said.

Goldfields reported a net profit after abnormals of A$14.19 million in the year to June 30, 1996 and a final dividend of three cents. The company said that although it was likely to declare a final dividend, in light of the lower profit from operations this dividend was unlikely to exceed five cents.
Goldfields is about 57 percent owned by RGC Ltd and holds about 87.2 percent of Pancontinental Mining Ltd.
At 2.35 p.m. (0335 GMT), Goldfields shares were one cent higher at A$2.30.
